events.text: In a pawnshop on a back street: a blade with a cracked scabbard, and on the scabbard, small and crowded, names. {echo_hands} of them, in different hands, and at the start of the list, very worn, the name {echo_name}. The pawnbroker says it {echo_heirloom}. He wants forty taels. It is worth everything.

choices.text: Buy it, and add your own name to the scabbard

effects.log: You carve your name at the end of the list with a borrowed knife. The blade is warm in your hand, as if it has been waiting.

choices.text: Read every name, then leave it for its next owner

effects.log: You read the names twice, the way you would read a family tree. Then you set it down. Some things are meant to keep travelling.

events.text: In {echo_craft_where} you find {echo_craft_thing}, very old and very good, with a maker's mark on it that stops your breath: the mark of {echo_name}. Your mark. Somebody has been taking very good care of it for {echo_years} years.

choices.text: Ask the owner where it came from

ok.log: "My grandmother bought it from the maker," the owner says, "and said it was the finest thing she ever owned." You have to sit down.

fail.log: Nobody remembers. That is all right. You remember, a little.

choices.text: Study how it was made, and remember how you did it

effects.log: You study it for an hour. Your hands remember things your head does not. Your next work is better than anything you have made in this life.

events.text: In the square of a market town there is a statue, weathered and covered in children: a martial artist with a raised sword, and on the plinth, '{echo_name}, who ended {echo_era}.' An old woman is leaving rice cakes at its feet, as her mother did, as her grandmother did.

effects.log: You put a rice cake beside hers and stand there a while. The statue has your nose. The sculptor got it right, this time.

choices.text: Ask the old woman what the town remembers

ok.log: She tells it the way it is told here: bigger, braver, kinder than it was. You let her. It is a better story than the truth.

fail.log: She is too busy with the rice cakes. A child climbs on your foot to reach the statue's sword. You lift them up.
